_purpose: Columns the approved TAD §3.1 names that are NOT YET in solution source, each ACCEPTED for now with an owner, a reason, the action that clears it, and a dated expiry. Read by scripts/verify-tad-coverage.py (C-TECH-066) and by nothing else.
_why: verify-tad-coverage.py is HARD: a column the approved architecture names and source does not hold is a schema defect that every other gate in this repository is structurally blind to, because an absent column is absent from both sides of every source-against-source comparison (IMP-0159). But phased delivery means some of those columns are legitimately not built yet, and a gate that is switched off because reality violates it is the gate-cannot-fail class arriving by the front door (contract/known-exceptions.json, _why). So absences are not waived silently: they are enumerated here, owned, dated, and re-reported on every run. This file deliberately mirrors known-exceptions.json's shape and its rule.
_not_a_waiver: A deferral suppresses the FAIL for the columns it names, never the report. Every run prints the deferred count in its summary line, and an expired deferral FAILS.
_required_fields: id, table, columns, reason, owner, clears_when, expires — all seven, on every entry. A deferral missing any of them FAILS the gate, and so does one whose `expires` is in the past or is not an ISO YYYY-MM-DD date. That is the point: an unowned or undated deferral is indistinguishable from a column nobody has noticed is missing, which is the exact state this gate was built to end.
_columns_field: Either the string "*", meaning every column TAD §3.1 names on that table (used when the TABLE itself does not exist in source yet), or an explicit array of column logical names. Prefer the array: "*" defers a whole table's schema, so it hides a column added to §3.1 afterwards.
_stale_entries_fail: A deferral that matches no absent §3.1 column FAILS as a dead promise — either the columns shipped or the TAD changed. Delete the entry when it is satisfied; a deferral file that accumulates satisfied entries becomes a blanket nobody reads.

deferrals.reason: TAD §3.1 groups it with `rev_wellbeinganswer1..n` and `rev_incomeband` as the score inputs (FR-013, FR-016). Source holds rev_wellbeinganswer1..rev_wellbeinganswer10 and rev_incomeband; nothing named rev_financialanswers exists, and the Phase 1 scoring engine shipped without reading it. Whether FR-013 needs a separate column at all, or is already satisfied by those eleven, is an architecture decision — and either answer needs a resolved WBS task before schema work, because automation #2's tasks are claimed complete (C-COM-002). Guessing a shape for a scoring input is exactly the class of invention this repository refuses (IMP-0011).
deferrals.clears_when: architect-agent rules on FR-013's inputs. If the eleven existing columns satisfy it: TAD §3.1 drops the name and this entry is deleted. If a real column is needed: it resolves to an accepted task or a change order, is built, and this entry is deleted.
deferrals.expiry_rationale: Short by design — a design ruling on an already-delivered automation, not new build work. It must resurface in four weeks rather than ride a phase date, because the scoring engine is live and every day it runs is a day it may be scoring on the wrong input set.

deferrals.reason: The five columns FR-023/FR-024/FR-025 need: check a new application against QuickBooks grant history at create time and record the prior grant's reference, date and amount on the APPLICATION. No accepted WBS task writes them. Task 4.3/4.4 (intake, claimed Done) do no QuickBooks lookup, and task 7.2 flags a possible double-pay on the PAYMENT row, not the application — so the application-side half of FR-023–025 is unquoted work today. That makes it a change-order or WBS-resolution decision for commercial-agent (C-COM-002) before any schema work, which is why these are deferred rather than built: building them would be delivery against no contract line.
deferrals.clears_when: commercial-agent resolves FR-023–025's application-side columns to an accepted WBS task or a change order. They are then built under it and this entry is deleted. If the decision is that the duplicate flag lives on Payment only, TAD §3.1's rev_application row is amended instead and this entry is deleted.
deferrals.expiry_rationale: Short by design — this is a commercial decision that needs no build to make, and it is the one deferral here with hours attached. Riding a phase date would let unquoted work sit undecided until the phase that cannot pay for it.

deferrals.expiry_rationale: Inherited from EX-003 and Phase 3's contractual due date, deliberately NOT shortened: the same absence is already owned and dated there, and two mechanisms holding different deadlines for one absence is how a deferral quietly outlives its exception. Same inheritance rule as TD-001–004.

_undelivered_requirements_purpose: Requirements the approved TAD's Appendix A traces to a response-document FIELD that the shipped artefact composes as a literal `null`. Recorded here, beside the column deferrals, because it is the same failure wearing a different shape: an approved document claiming coverage that source does not supply. _undelivered_requirements_is_read_by_no_: CORRECTED 2026-08-28 (improvement review 39, IMP-0462) — THIS KEY SAID THE OPPOSITE OF THE TRUTH, and it was the most emphatic sentence in the file. `scripts/verify-tad-coverage.py` DOES read `undelivered_requirements`. Improvement review 38 made it a control the same day this key was written, and the key was not updated: assertion (d) acquits a null response key when a register entry names it in `response_fields`, and assertion (f) FAILS a dead promise — an entry naming a field that is no longer composed as a literal null in any flow's OK document. Every entry is validated for its seven fields and for a non-past ISO `expires`, and an EXPIRED entry fails the HARD `tad-coverage` build step. So this is a CONTROL, not merely a written record. THREE THINGS THAT FOLLOW, each of which has already cost something. FIRST: `response_fields` must hold LEAF KEY NAMES (`averageAmountRequested`), never dotted paths (`exceptionalFundingSummary.averageAmountRequested`) — a path matches no composed key, so it fails assertion (f) as a dead promise, which cost one measurement on 2026-08-28. SECOND: when only SOME of an entry's fields ship, NARROW the entry rather than deleting it — deleting it removes the only dated record that the rest is undelivered, which is the defect the entry exists to prevent (IMP-0462, correcting IMP-0459's proposal to delete UR-001/UR-002/UR-003; UR-001 was genuinely satisfied and deleted, UR-002 and UR-003 were narrowed). THIRD: a leaf key name shared by two metrics is matched by NAME, so one entry naming it acquits every occurrence, including a second metric's — improvement review 39 makes the gate REPORT that multiplicity on every verdict, and binding an acquittal to one composing action is deferred until TAD A-FLOW-08 settles these entries. CURRENT STATE AT THE TIME OF THIS CORRECTION, verified by running the gate: it exits 1 with FOUR assertion-(f) dead-promise violations, because a concurrent dispatch has shipped all four money measures, so UR-002 and UR-003 now match nothing. Clearing them is DELIVERY's action and is deliberately not done here: deleting the entries without correcting TAD Appendix A's rows in the same change produces the mirror-image overclaim (a traceability row reading UNDELIVERED for a field that has a producer), and improvement-agent does not own this register's entries. Owner: whichever dispatch shipped the measures, paired with the Appendix A erratum. PRIOR TEXT, SUPERSEDED AND RETAINED so a reader can see what changed (it was accurate about the `deferrals` array and wrong about this key): STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ABOUT THIS KEY. `scripts/verify-tad-coverage.py` reads ONLY the `deferrals` array above, and it matches every entry there against an ABSENT TAD §3.1 COLUMN. These three gaps are keys inside a response document serialised into a Memo column that EXISTS (`rev_resultjson` on `rev_roundstatisticsresult`), so there is no absent §3.1 column for them to match. Putting them in `deferrals` was not assumed unworkable, it was MEASURED: the gate exits 1 with `defers nothing: no absent TAD §3.1 column on rev_roundstatisticsresult matches it`, which is a HARD `C-TECH-066` failure that would block every build until the entry was removed again. So they sit in their own key, which that gate ignores by construction. An entry in an unread key is a WRITTEN RECORD, NOT A CONTROL: the only things standing between these three and being forgotten again are TAD Appendix A's corrected rows, TAD §11 A-R51, and the per-entry `verify_by` command below that a human runs. `logs/improvement-log.jsonl` IMP-0451's own `proposed_change` asks `improvement-agent` to extend the gate to Appendix A, which is what would make this key checked; that promotion is not architect-agent's to apply.

_undelivered_requirements_the_remaining_: READ THIS BEFORE EITHER ENTRY BELOW. Both remaining entries have the same single cause, ground-truthed on 2026-08-28 against Microsoft's own workflow-definition-language function reference: the language's math functions are `add, div, max, min, mod, mul, pow, rand, range, sub`, and `add` takes exactly TWO operands. So a sum over a FIXED operand count is expressible by nesting `add()` — which is why FR-060's five-operand total-row count IS delivered — and a sum over a VARIABLE-LENGTH array is not expressible at all. Every field still `null` below is a mean over a filtered subset of the round, and that is the whole of what they have in common. This is NOT a sizing question any more: three mechanisms exist (an `Apply to each` accumulation, proven but ~900 sequential action executions that would break TAD §3.3 point 5's 'reads as seconds old'; `xpath(xml(...),'sum(...)')`, one action but unverified on this tenant and a silent `0` on malformed input would put a WRONG money figure on a board pack; or reopening ADR-030's rejection of a Dataverse Custom API). Choosing between them trades a load-bearing property of an approved design against an unverified platform contract, so it is `architect-agent`'s decision, carried as TAD A-FLOW-08 and TAD §0.8.1. `development-agent` deliberately did NOT pick one.
_ur_002_and_ur_003_cleared: UR-002 AND UR-003 CLEARED 2026-08-28 (feature:trustee-portal-visual-refresh, development-agent, wbs:6.9), on each entry's own `clears_when` and paired with the TAD Appendix A correction in the SAME change, which is what `_undelivered_requirements_is_read_by_no_gate` names as the condition for clearing them. Both `clears_when` conditions were met in order: `architect-agent` ruled on the summation mechanism (TAD Revision 6, ADR-039 — a guarded `xpath(xml(concat(…join(…)…)),'sum(/r/v)')`, A-FLOW-08 RESOLVED), the reviewer ruled on the disclosure question UR-003's own `reason` predicted (TAD OQ-043, answered `k = 5` on 2026-08-28), and the flow now composes all four measures. FIVE THINGS A LATER READER SHOULD KNOW RATHER THAN INFER. FIRST: the measures are not unconditionally emitted. Each is `{ value, population }` where its own population is ≥ k, and the JSON literal `null` below it, with the row's `count` still published — so a break type with fewer than five costed applications legitimately shows no money figures, which is intended behaviour and not a residual gap (TAD §6.3.5, §3.3's worked example). SECOND: `k` comes from the `rev_setting` row `RoundStatisticsMoneyMeasureMinimumPopulation`, seeded 5 in all three environment settings files this dispatch. An ABSENT row withholds all four measures — fail-safe, but not the approved state, so the seeding is not optional. THIRD: verification reached V1 only (definition-level — JSON valid, the document simulated over a synthetic round in six scenarios including k unseeded and k mistyped, 47-assertion regression test at `src/tests/solutions/RoundStatisticsContract.Tests.ps1`, four mutations reproduced). NO RUN HAS PRODUCED ANY OF THESE FIGURES, and `xml()`/`xpath()` have never executed on this tenant — carried as OPEN assumption A-FLOW-11 with its marker at every `Compose_*_sum`. FOURTH: `_undelivered_requirements_the_remaining_two_are_a_platform_limit_not_scope` above is now SUPERSEDED and one clause of it was measured WRONG. Its account of the WDL is still correct — there is no `sum()` over a variable-length array and `add` is still binary; `xpath` reaches XPath 1.0's own `sum()`, which is a different language reached through a string. But its characterisation of that route's failure mode as 'a silent `0` on malformed input' is only half of it: measured against libxml2 on 2026-08-28, XPath 1.0 `sum()` returns `0` over an EMPTY node set and `NaN` over a node set containing ANY empty element, and `NaN` is not valid JSON, so the unguarded form takes all thirteen metrics off the screen rather than putting one wrong figure on a board pack. Both failure modes are removed at source rather than watched for. FIFTH: FR-060's `averageAmountRequested` is the SUM of `rev_amountrequested` and `rev_additionalamountrequested` per row, which is a reading of SDD FR-060's '(including exceptional funding)' and of TAD §3.1's own column-to-requirement mapping — carried as OPEN assumption A-FLOW-12, and one expression to change if the charity means the base ask alone.
_ur_001_cleared: UR-001 CLEARED 2026-08-28 (feature:trustee-portal-visual-refresh, development-agent, wbs:6.9) — FR-058's `applicationsPerDay` is now composed from a real figure by `Compose_applications_per_day`, which divides the round's application count by whole elapsed days since `rev_roundfinance.rev_roundopenedon`, floored at 1 so the round's opening day cannot divide by zero. SECOND: verification reached V1 only (definition-level — JSON valid, response document simulated over a synthetic 434-row round in four scenarios, 35-assertion regression test at `src/tests/solutions/RoundStatisticsContract.Tests.ps1`). NO RUN HAS PRODUCED THIS FIGURE. `rev_roundopenedon` is entered by hand and may be empty in DEV, in which case the flow emits `null` for the whole metric by design (TAD §3.3 point 3 — an absence, never a zero), so the first live run may legitimately show nothing here and that is not a defect.
